per_token_model.note: Energy = fixed + per 1k input tokens + per 1k output tokens (reasoning included), fitted exactly to the three prompt sizes in Jegham et al. 2025 (arXiv 2505.09598 v6, Table 4: 100/300, 1k/1k, 10k/1.5k tokens). Inputs far beyond 10k tokens, such as long video, are extrapolated linearly, which likely understates them.

lifecycle.note: Adds to the operational per-task energy (mid-size model): training and development (multiplier m on operational energy), hardware manufacturing and buildings, full carbon accounting, and full water (on-site + electricity generation + chip manufacturing). Method and sources: docs/LIFECYCLE.md.

low.why: training amortised over a year at very large volume; market-based carbon (Google 94 g/kWh) plus Google's measured hardware share; low electricity water (Ai2)

central.why: fleet ratios of training to inference (Meta 10:20:70, Google 2/5:3/5); manufacturing about 12.5% of operational energy (IEA); grid-average carbon (about 414 g/kWh); US electricity water (Li et al.); chip water from IEA's share

high.why: a very large training run (IEA's largest, about 310 GWh) at the same volume, or a model with few users; high electricity water
